title: Volume and Capacity of Cubes and Cuboids
seo_title: Volume and Capacity – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the volume of cubes and cuboids by counting cubes and by formula; relate volume to capacity in litres; solve problems on volume and capacity. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on volume of cubes and cuboids, cubic units, the formula length × breadth × height, litres and millilitres, and tank problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Volume is the space inside a solid. It is measured in cubic units: cm³ and m³.
  • Volume of a cuboid = length × breadth × height. Volume of a cube = side × side × side.
  • Capacity is how much a container holds. 1 cm³ = 1 ml and 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre.

Examples

Example

Cuboid 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm

8 × 5 × 3

Answer: 120 cm³

Example

A tank holds 6,000 cm³

6,000 ÷ 1,000

Answer: 6 litres

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the lengthsMultiply the three lengths.
Writing cm² for volumeVolume is in cm³.
Forgetting to change unitsAll lengths must be in the same unit.

faq.q: What is the difference between volume and capacity?
faq.a: Volume is the space a solid takes up; capacity is how much a container can hold.

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes make up this cuboid?
items.e: One layer has 2 rows of 4 cubes = 8 cubes. There are 3 layers: 8 × 3 = 24. Count the hidden cubes too (only 18 cubes can be seen).

items.q: The cuboid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: One layer has 3 rows of 3 cubes = 9 cubes. There are 2 layers: 9 × 2 = 18. Count the hidden cubes too (only 14 cubes can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes make up this cuboid?
items.e: One layer has 2 rows of 5 cubes = 10 cubes. There are 2 layers: 10 × 2 = 20. Count the hidden cubes too (only 16 cubes can be seen).

items.q: The cuboid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes make up this cuboid?
items.e: One layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes = 4 cubes. There are 4 layers: 4 × 4 = 16. Count the hidden cubes too (only 13 cubes can be seen).

items.q: The cube is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: One layer has 3 rows of 3 cubes = 9 cubes. There are 3 layers: 9 × 3 = 27. Count the hidden cubes too (only 19 cubes can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes are used to build this solid?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 3 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 12 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 9 can be seen).

items.q: The solid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 10 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 9 can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes are used to build this solid?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 2 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 13 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 10 can be seen).

items.q: The solid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 14 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 9 can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.q: How many 1-cm cubes are used to build this solid?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 22 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 16 can be seen).

items.q: The solid is made of 1-cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Add the cubes in each column: 2 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 24 cubes. Some cubes are hidden under or behind others (only 16 can be seen). Each cube is 1 cm³.

items.q: How many more 1-cm cubes are needed to make a cube with edges of 3 cm?
items.e: A cube with edges of 3 cm has 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cubes. The solid has 3 + 6 + 9 = 18 cubes. 27 − 18 = 9 more.

items.q: How many more 1-cm cubes are needed to make a cuboid 3 cm long, 2 cm wide and 3 cm high?
items.e: The cuboid needs 3 × 2 × 3 = 18 cubes. The solid has 3 + 7 = 10 cubes. 18 − 10 = 8 more.

items.q: How many more 1-cm cubes are needed to make a cube with edges of 3 cm?
items.e: A cube with edges of 3 cm has 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cubes. The solid has 7 cubes (one is hidden at the back). 27 − 7 = 20 more. (1 more cube would only make a cube with edges of 2 cm.)

items.q: Both solids are made of 1-cm cubes. How much greater is the volume of Solid A than Solid B?
items.e: Solid A: 3 × 2 × 3 = 18 cm³. Solid B: 3 + 5 + 6 = 14 cm³. 18 − 14 = 4 cm³. Count the hidden cubes in both.

items.q: Both solids are made of 1-cm cubes. What is their total volume?
items.e: Solid A: 2 × 3 × 2 = 12 cm³. Solid B: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 cm³. Total = 12 + 6 = 18 cm³.

items.q: A cuboid is made of 1-cm cubes. Each layer has 4 rows of 6 cubes. There are 3 layers. What is its volume?
items.e: One layer = 4 × 6 = 24 cubes. 3 layers = 24 × 3 = 72 cubes = 72 cm³.

items.q: Usman fills a box with 1-cm cubes. The bottom layer has 15 cubes. The box holds 4 layers. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: 15 cubes in each layer × 4 layers = 60 cubes. The volume is 60 cm³.

items.q: Ada builds a cube with edges of 4 cm from 1-cm cubes. How many cubes does she use?
items.e: 4 × 4 = 16 cubes in each layer. There are 4 layers: 16 × 4 = 64 cubes.

items.q: What is the volume of this cuboid?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 × 2 × 12 = 12 × 12 = 144 m³. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: m³.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 11 m long. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge of a cube is 11 m, so V = 11 × 11 × 11 = 121 × 11 = 1,331 m³.

items.q: What is the volume of this cuboid?

items.q: What is the volume of this cuboid?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 2 = 12 × 2 = 24 cu in. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu in.

items.q: The base of a cuboid has an area of 15 sq cm. The prism is 12 cm tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h, where B is the area of the base: 15 × 12 = 180 cm³. Think of 12 layers with 15 cubes in each.

items.q: 7 litres = ? cm³
items.e: 1 litre = 1,000 cm³, so 7 litres = 7 × 1,000 = 7,000 cm³.

items.q: 12 litres = ? cm³
items.e: 1 litre = 1,000 cm³, so 12 litres = 12 × 1,000 = 12,000 cm³.

items.q: 250 ml = ? cm³
items.e: 1 ml = 1 cm³, so 250 ml = 250 cm³. Do not multiply or divide by 1,000.

items.q: 600 ml = ? cm³
items.e: 1 ml = 1 cm³, so 600 ml = 600 cm³. Do not multiply or divide by 1,000.

items.q: 5,000 cm³ = ? litres
items.e: 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre, so divide by 1,000: 5,000 ÷ 1,000 = 5 litres.

items.q: 8,000 cm³ = ? litres
items.e: 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre, so divide by 1,000: 8,000 ÷ 1,000 = 8 litres.

items.q: 20,000 cm³ = ? litres
items.e: 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre, so divide by 1,000: 20,000 ÷ 1,000 = 20 litres.

items.q: Write 2,450 cm³ in litres and millilitres.
items.e: 2,450 cm³ = 2,450 ml = 2,000 ml + 450 ml = 2 litres 450 ml. The thousands are the litres.

items.q: Write 3,080 cm³ in litres and millilitres.
items.e: 3,080 cm³ = 3,080 ml = 3,000 ml + 80 ml = 3 litres 80 ml. The thousands are the litres.

items.q: Write 1,605 cm³ in litres and millilitres.
items.e: 1,605 cm³ = 1,605 ml = 1,000 ml + 605 ml = 1 litre 605 ml. The thousands are the litres.

items.q: 1 litre 80 ml = ? cm³
items.e: 1 litre = 1,000 ml. 1,000 ml + 80 ml = 1,080 ml = 1,080 cm³. (80 ml is not 800 ml.)

items.q: Which is equal to 1 litre 50 ml?
items.e: 1 litre 50 ml = 1,000 ml + 50 ml = 1,050 ml = 1,050 cm³. 1,500 cm³ would be 1 litre 500 ml.

items.q: The water in the tank is 20 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 40 × 30 × 20 = 24,000 cm³ = 24 litres.

items.q: The water in the tank is 35 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 60 × 40 × 35 = 84,000 cm³ = 84 litres.

items.q: The water in the tank is 28 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 50 × 25 × 28 = 35,000 cm³ = 35 litres.

items.q: How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 60 − 35 = 25 cm high. 50 × 40 × 25 = 50,000 cm³ = 50 litres.

items.q: How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 45 − 25 = 20 cm high. 40 × 30 × 20 = 24,000 cm³ = 24 litres.

items.q: How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 40 − 15 = 25 cm high. 60 × 30 × 25 = 45,000 cm³ = 45 litres.

items.q: A tank 40 cm long, 40 cm wide and 50 cm high contains 32 litres of water. How many more litres of water are needed to fill it completely?
items.e: Capacity = 40 × 40 × 50 = 80,000 cm³ = 80 litres. More water needed = 80 − 32 = 48 litres.

items.q: A tank is 50 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. It contains 27 litres 500 ml of water. How much more water is needed to fill it?
items.e: Capacity = 50 × 30 × 40 = 60,000 cm³ = 60 litres. 60 litres − 27 litres 500 ml = 32 litres 500 ml.

items.q: A tank is 60 cm long, 50 cm wide and 40 cm high. It is 34 full of water. How many litres of water are in it?
items.e: Capacity = 60 × 50 × 40 = 120,000 cm³ = 120 litres. 34 of 120 litres = 120 ÷ 4 × 3 = 90 litres.

items.q: A tank is 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. It is 23 full of water. How many litres of water are in it?
items.e: Capacity = 50 × 40 × 30 = 60,000 cm³ = 60 litres. 23 of 60 litres = 60 ÷ 3 × 2 = 40 litres.

items.q: Mrs Musa's fish tank is 25 full. It has 24 litres of water in it. How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank?
items.e: 2 units = 24 litres, so 1 unit = 12 litres. The empty part is 3 units = 3 × 12 = 36 litres. (The full tank is 5 units = 60 litres.)

items.q: A tank is 14 full of water. After 30 litres of water is added, it is 34 full. What is the capacity of the tank?
items.e: The 30 litres fills 34 − 14 = 24 of the tank. 2 units = 30 litres, so 1 unit = 15 litres. Capacity = 4 units = 4 × 15 = 60 litres.

items.q: Tank A has 3 times as much water as Tank B. Together they hold 48 litres of water. How much water is in Tank A?
items.e: 4 units = 48 litres, so 1 unit = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 litres. Tank A = 3 units = 3 × 12 = 36 litres. (16 litres is 48 ÷ 3.)

items.q: Tank P has 15 litres more water than Tank Q. Together they hold 75 litres of water. How much water is in Tank Q?
items.e: Take away the extra 15 litres: 75 − 15 = 60 litres. This is 2 equal parts, so Tank Q = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 litres. Tank P = 30 + 15 = 45 litres.

items.q: An empty tank is 60 cm long, 40 cm wide and 50 cm high. A tap fills it at 8 litres per minute. How long does it take to fill the tank?
items.e: Capacity = 60 × 40 × 50 = 120,000 cm³ = 120 litres. Time = 120 ÷ 8 = 15 min.

items.q: A tank 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 45 cm high has water 15 cm deep. Water flows in from a tap at 6 litres per minute. How long will it take to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 45 − 15 = 30 cm high: 50 × 40 × 30 = 60,000 cm³ = 60 litres. Time = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 min. (15 min would fill the whole tank of 90 litres.)

items.q: A tank 40 cm long, 30 cm wide and 25 cm high is full of water. Chidi pours all the water into bottles. Each bottle holds 750 ml. How many bottles can he fill?
The school's water tank is 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 60 cm high. It is 40% full. How many litres of water are in it?
items.e: Capacity = 50 × 40 × 60 = 120,000 cm³ = 120 litres. 40% of 120 litres = 120 ÷ 100 × 40 = 48 litres.

items.q: Uche's fish tank is 24 cm long, 15 cm wide and 20 cm high. The water in it is 13 cm deep. What is the volume of the water in litres and millilitres?
items.e: Water = 24 × 15 × 13 = 360 × 13 = 4,680 cm³ = 4,680 ml = 4 litres 680 ml. Use the depth (13 cm), not the height.

items.q: Mr Bello's tank is 60 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. It is full of water. He fills 3 pails with water from the tank. Each pail holds 8 litres 500 ml. How much water is left in the tank?
items.e: Capacity = 60 × 40 × 30 = 72,000 cm³ = 72 litres. Water used = 3 × 8 litres 500 ml = 25 litres 500 ml. 72 litres − 25 litres 500 ml = 46 litres 500 ml.
